note: Slot 1 (revised 11/10 for pace: the scene now opens on the hand he hides until noon, so the reader dreads the Reading):  the fate c04.12b on the page at a Reading at the noon ford (never the knee, never mended, never a lecture); the knee cleared for nothing new (walking only). Rae's silence paid c05.13b: oxen only, no song, the bell ragged. The sword stays Maelis's under the salt (no inventory change); the inscription stays one word. Hollis's opinion is thread 13; the rein for Thistle is thread 15 and clears no riding. The register came out bittersweet with the Book's warmth round it. No callback fired; c06.1a and c05.7a wait. Kept off: the rider, the camp, anything of the weir.
next_must_know: From now every grip is three fingers and a thumb, the stick held high, the point stopping where the wrist stops; slot 2's Overwall stones go from that hand. Rae has not spoken to anyone but the oxen today; the road lie in slot 2 is where her voice comes back for the road's sake. Tonight's camp needs a field wall. The Reading is done for the week.

threads.who_knows: Hollis, Darrow, Wren, the kitchen; the reader. The drink: Hollis, Darrow, the reader. The new grip: the whole company (06:s1).
threads.note: 06:s1: Hollis set the Captain's hand on the hilt: the Seated Blade's grip is three fingers and a thumb now, and he called the lost fingers an argument finished.

threads.who_knows: Rae; Darrow (he has seen her at the dealer's in Coldmere, 05:s4, and knows Rae has paid her keep since the fair); the dealer; the company heard him say he wants a rein for her in the spring (06:s1); the reader.
threads.note: 06:s1: Darrow told Maelis there is a grey in Coldmere he will want a rein for in the spring; she said a rein is two fingers' work and a saddle is for the spring.

note: Between 1, Rae's silence after the fork answered on the page: she knows the river road's farms and drove past with her bell stopped; the true part is that she was glad he chose his own (her carter's rule of everybody or nobody broken in her own chest); he gave back his hidden reason (he chose north so the grey cloaks would not question her again) and owned deciding for her; she set the term why-first at the next fork (c06.2a). The rag stays in the bell. Nothing of the calling, the salt sack or the uncle's book. Hollis heard; Wren asleep; Maelis out of earshot.
next_must_know: Rae and Darrow are square on the fork; she will drive and talk again. At the next road decision Darrow owes her his reason first, aloud (c06.2a). The rag is still in her bell.

threads.note: 06:between-1: Rae said she was glad at the fork when he chose north for his own, against her rule of carrying for everybody or nobody, and told him she gave him the road, never the carter; she set him why-first at the next fork.

note: Slot 2 (revised 11/10 for pace: Darrow keeps lookout and counts the quarter hour while the lie is laid; the scene ends on the empty skyline): the rider on the skyline (thread 23's second plant), one and not a column, keeping the mile; Rae's road lie at the spring, Wren counting it in the epigraph's words; Darrow kept his promise at the fork (c06.2a fired). The lesson over the wall is moved to the slot's invitation (the plan had it in both): the scene ends with Hollis's hat on the far side of the wall, and if Darrow answers, the Between opens on Hollis and fires c05.9a; if not, Hollis lobs stones alone till the light goes. The rider stays 'the rider' (the miller's man said he; nobody has seen a face). No tally: the pull was named and let be, not a chase forgone. Maelis kept off slot 4's line about waiting.
next_must_know: The rider has seen them stop and go and keeps a mile; the road lie lies at the spring dip behind them (slot 8's interlude reads it from the other side and believes it). Hollis's hat is over the wall. Slot 3: the mill-track inn in the hill country, a drover's word about the rider paying well, the family with the lame ox; ends on the small choice.

threads.who_knows: The whole company has seen the rider on the skyline a mile behind at dusk (06:s2); Darrow and Hollis tie it to the miller's man's rider (05:s7); the reader. Unnamed; nobody has seen a face; who sent the rider, or why alive, nobody knows.
threads.note: 06:s2: second plant: one rider on a long-legged horse, a mile back on the skyline at dusk, stopping when they stop, walking a horse shod for speed.

note: Slot 2's invitation taken: Hollis's second lesson (Overwall) played as the Between, c05.9a fired; the die gave a partial: the second stone in off the wall, and Hollis's right to tell it clean is the cost. Darrow told Hollis he was right about the fingers. One line of the rider out of sight doing the same sum, unexplained. The keepsake of Tale 1 was not touched (one callback a block).
next_must_know: Overwall is taught on the page as a throw at an unseen mark by where it must come down; Hollis will improve the story. Slot 3: the mill-track inn in the hill country, a drover's word about the rider, the family with the lame ox; the small choice at its end.

threads.note: 06:between-2: Hollis taught Overwall at the camp wall by ear, named it, and claimed the right to tell it clean; Darrow told him he was right about the fingers.

note: Slot 3 as planned: the drover's rider (stood a round at the landing three nights back, drank water, asked off a list, asked how far a man with a stick walks in a day: the duelist's eye on feet); the road names the company as a thing (the Thorne cart carries for anybody; a captain goes with it who would not kneel); the river family off the side lanes asks for Hob. The boy with one boot and his foot in sacking is the shoe Rae named on the box (06:between-1), shown, never said. Darrow sees bedding on a cart and remembers the ford's carts in one line (thread 3 touched, nothing revealed). Rae lends the ox and gives him the day: her road, his decision. The armed telling rule was left for its own place.
next_must_know: The small choice is open; the next scene opens on his answer. The family's boy has Maelis's wrapping on his foot. The rider has been asking the road about his walking.

threads.note: 06:s3: a drover at the hill inn met the rider at the landing three nights back: stood a round, drank water, asked off a list (captain, carter, Mender), and asked how far a man with a stick walks in a day.

note: Darrow's own answer to slot 3's small choice, played: he gave Rae the call (c06.6, priced as option 1, Banner +1), she chose out loud to lend Hob and the day (her Book II growth: choosing aloud), Hollis objected for the rider and gave in, and gave the boy his right boot (Mercy, his own); Rae took the rag out of her bell, which pays Between 1's 'I went by them like one'. The bell ringing on frost is the cost Darrow saw and let be; slot 4's noon meeting follows from it.
next_must_know: Slot 4 opens in a clause on c06.6a: first light over the hill, Hob in the river family's cart, Rae's cart on Dun and the mule, the lame ox behind unladen, the bell ringing, half a day's pace; the boy in Hollis's right boot stuffed with straw. The rag is in Rae's pocket.

threads.note: 06:between-3: given the call by Darrow, Rae chose out loud to lend Hob and the day to a river family, and took the rag out of her bell: a carter carries for anybody and lets the road hear her doing it.

note: Slot 4 as planned: the rider seen plainly (a woman, slight, six buttons, a horse that never shifts; unnamed). The tally moment went held: the old pull took him twenty paces onto the meadow, he read her ground and stood square instead of going on (a pre-echo of the weir's stone). The cost with the company is Wren's: he went without telling her first, the first time he has broken it; it is carried into slot 6's invitation (her want) rather than charged now. The bell rang all day by Rae's choice and the rider found them beside it, not behind. Colour cold: the warmth in him was the old speed's.
next_must_know: The rider has been seen as a woman and a duelist; nobody has her name. Wren's count: told first twice, not once (slot 6's invitation is her asking). Rae's invitation (the sack) is open tonight; if he lets it pass she tells him at slot 5's start. The family's village is close; the mill is beyond it.

threads.who_knows: The whole company has seen the rider plainly: a slight woman on a long-legged horse who sits like a duelist and does not close (06:s4); Darrow and Hollis tie her to the miller's man's rider (05:s7); the reader. Unnamed; who sent her, or why alive, nobody knows.
threads.note: 06:s4: the rider seen plainly at noon across a frozen water-meadow: a woman, six buttons, hands that never moved; she looked at Darrow alone and rode off at a walk.

note: Slot 4's invitation taken: Rae told him the corner before the mill (r.b2.rae_tells fired; rae_market_told true by her choice): the sack, the mill, people on the coast who pay for what the road knows, a lamp for every road; never opened; the right question (what she carried for them at the House) refused for tonight. Nothing named: no Market, no Saltreach, no uncle. Darrow gave back his want on the meadow: Aldric's face.
next_must_know: Darrow knows the drop and the coast's buyers and that Rae carried for them up the mountain; he has promised nothing and pressed nothing. The sack is under the cart for the mill (Fri night, slot 6). Wren will weigh it; she does not know.

threads.who_knows: Rae; her uncle Hale, the lamp at Coldmere; Darrow now knows the corner (06:between-4): the sack goes to the mill and down the road to people on the coast who pay for what the road knows, and she carried for them up the mountain; nobody else in the company; the reader.
threads.note: 06:between-4: the corner told before the mill, by her choice; the right question (what she carried up the mountain) left for some night with nobody on the hill behind them.

note: Slot 5 as planned: the summons under his writ (exact to comedy: four measured nails; 'which is to say not tomorrow'; 'less time to ask than this has taken to write'); Darrow's read (Insight success: no lie, means what it says); the company's argument each with a point; Darrow asks and listens to the end instead of deciding first. New Annals entry realm.forms (common), spoken here: the summoned chooses where on the ground he stands, which slot 6's stone pays. Level 9 shown in the box.
next_must_know: The small choice is open (sworn_unsworn). Under the forms he chooses where on her ground he stands: slot 6's stone. Rae reads the weir at the mill tomorrow night when she takes the sack in (the drop). Wren's invitation is slot 6's.

threads.note: 06:s5: the summons nailed under his writ: under the forms, the weir below the mill, first light on the second morning, alone, a question; unsigned, a duelist's hand.
